question: Per director_mandate.allocation: can the audited parameterized inherited carrier (research/experiments/EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440/harness/audited_spider/kernel.py, git blob b15ed8487e2d1326df4ca64fb4c7b6e5a0ebf796, sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72) be landed into the shipped kernel src/spider/kernel.py through the sanctioned promotion path so that the shipped execution path contains a concrete parameterized mechanism that an inherited procedure visibly instantiates and executes (distill_parameterized -> resolve -> execute -> verify), together with a companion known-negative refusal certificate, satisfying blocker B1 and the pre-freeze executable-mechanism requirement of readiness condition (1) - rather than once more running the four-arm economics benchmark on a kernel that still emits literals below the execution threshold? The mandated comparison is between the SHIPPED kernel after the sanctioned landing and the shipped literal pre-repair kernel at the same min_confidence=0.8 gate, on the same observed treatment.
hypothesis: On the shipped import path (PYTHONPATH=src, module spider.kernel), after the audited carrier blob b15ed848 (sha256 718efa6a...) is landed as src/spider/kernel.py on the Product branch as the only code delta, the shipped kernel (a) exposes distill_parameterized and induces a parameterized mechanism with confidence >= 0.8 from >= 2 consistent successful same-intent observations; (b) resolves unseen in-support identifiers to ResolutionStatus.EXECUTABLE and re-verifies True after a real, credential-free localhost HTTP execute, for two independent identifier families (docs: doc-555; records: rec-999) never present in the induction observations; (c) refuses missing-parameter, out-of-support and wrong-intent requests with bound_action=null and typed reasons ('missing required parameter', 'outside inferred support', 'no applicable validated mechanism'); (d) the pre-repair literal distill() path alone (hardcoded confidence 0.5) yields resolution EXPLORE with bound_action=null on the same requests; and (e) the exact three shell commands product-promote.yml runs over the landing delta (python -m compileall -q src scripts; python scripts/validate_repo.py; PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v) all succeed, with the delta confined to the allowed code roots and all frozen interpretation artifacts byte-identical.
falsifier: Any one of the following falsifies the hypothesis: (F-a) after landing, sha256(src/spider/kernel.py) != 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72 or git hash-object != b15ed8487e2d1326df4ca64fb4c7b6e5a0ebf796, or it equals the pre-landing sha256 46929b3a951df48d7f9d1fd850871073c0d91c1868aa117e13d389fe274e8d61; (F-b) the shipped module cannot expose a parameterized mechanism that resolves unseen in-support identifiers to EXECUTABLE (i.e. positive round-trip fails for either family); (F-c) post-execution verify() does not return True for either family; (F-d) any of the three known-negative categories is not refused with bound_action=null and a non-empty typed reason; (F-e) the literal ablation path executes (EXECUTABLE) instead of EXPLORE at min_confidence=0.8; (F-f) the landing delta touches a path outside the allowed code roots, breaks any existing tests/test_kernel.py test, or fails compileall/validate_repo/unittest; (F-g) any freeze_artifact listed in spec.freeze_artifacts changes sha256 between freeze and the confirmatory measurement. A failure of F-a/F-b/F-d is scientific FALSIFIES for this landing; a failure of F-c/F-e/F-f/F-g is MIXED (the shipped parameterized path may still work, but either causality, landability or interpretation-binding is not established).

baselines.description: The pre-repair literal path: the landed kernel's own distill() (hardcoded confidence 0.5, no parameter_slots) upserted into a fresh registry, resolved at the same min_confidence=0.8 on exactly the same context and params as the treatment arm. Expected: ResolutionStatus.EXPLORE, bound_action=null, reason 'candidate exists but confidence is below execution threshold' for both families. Metric: M-ABLATION-LITERAL-EXECUTABLE-COUNT == 0. This isolates the parameterized induction + support-guard as the cause of execution, not the substrate or the server.
baselines.frozen_source: landed src/spider/kernel.py (same file as treatment; only the code path differs)

baselines.description: A fresh SpiderKernel over an empty registry is queried with the same intent/context/params. Expected: ResolutionStatus.UNKNOWN, bound_action=null, reason 'no applicable validated mechanism'. Metric: M-NULL-EMPTY-EXECUTABLE-COUNT == 0. Rules out the harness/server manufacturing an EXECUTABLE result without a mechanism.

The pre-landing shipped kernel, sha256 46929b3a951df48d7f9d1fd850871073c0d91c1868aa117e13d389fe274e8d61 (git blob cfec98660b0277ccbf295e8a4119e8d81ddccf50), which has no distill_parameterized and whose resolve() silently drops candidates with missing parameters. Used only to pin the before-state identity of the shipped file (F-a) and to state the exact diff being promoted; its own behavior is already established by B1 at source and is not re-measured as the confirmatory outcome.

positive_control: PC-PARAM-ROUNDTRIP: for each family independently (docs: train doc-102/doc-247/doc-391; records: train rec-514/rec-628/rec-736), distill_parameterized over three successful real-HTTP observations must produce a mechanism with confidence 0.9 (>= 0.8) and support descriptors; then resolve('update_resource', {'authenticated': true, 'role': 'owner'}, {<id-slot>: <unseen>, 'value': 'draft-7'}) for the unseen in-support identifier (doc-555 / rec-999, absent from induction) must return EXECUTABLE with a non-null bound_action whose url targets the unseen identifier; executing that bound_action over the localhost server must return the expected JSON and verify(mechanism_id, response_body, params) must return True. Expected: M-PC-ROUNDTRIP-EXECUTABLE-COUNT == 2 and M-PC-ROUNDTRIP-VERIFY-COUNT == 2. PC-SUPPORT-BOUNDARY: the same mechanisms must accept the unseen in-support identifiers and refuse the near-miss out-of-support identifiers (doc-55, rec-55) with reason 'outside inferred support'; expected accept=2, refuse=2. This control proves the treatment is live and that the support guard is sensitive rather than trivially permissive.
null_control: N-EMPTY-REGISTRY (see baselines) plus N-ABSTENTION-NO-REQUEST: for every refused resolution (known negatives and near-misses), no HTTP request may be sent by the treatment path (the resolve result has bound_action=null, so nothing is executed); M-ABSTENTION-HTTP-REQUESTS == 0. This guards against the harness executing a fallback or the server logging traffic that should not exist.
measurement_validity: Shipped-path identity: the measurement MUST import spider.kernel with PYTHONPATH=src from the repository root, not a vendored harness copy; the harness resolves the module file path via spider.kernel.__file__ and records it. If it resolves outside src/spider, the run is MEASUREMENT_INVALID.

Substrate is credential-free and deterministic: a stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer bound to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, no external network, no model calls, no randomness. Each family uses one fixed base_url/port for both induction and test so the parameterized URL template is internally consistent.
Real execution is required: verify() is measured on the actual HTTP response body, not on a replayed or fabricated dict. Raw response bodies are preserved.
Ablation and null controls run in fresh registries on the same landed kernel, so they cannot be contaminated by the treatment registry.

Unseen identifiers are declared absent from the induction set by construction (doc-555 not in {doc-102,doc-247,doc-391}; rec-999 not in {rec-514,rec-628,rec-736}) and are in-support by the inferred grammar ^doc\-[0-9]{3}$ / ^rec\-[0-9]{3}$; near-misses (doc-55, rec-55) differ only in digit count.
Test isolation: the new test file creates its mechanisms in a tempfile-backed registry, not the committed src/spider/mechanisms.jsonl, so promotion does not mutate shipped data.

Promotion landability is measured locally by running the exact commands product-promote.yml runs over the delta; the main-branch application itself is a scheduled, connection-gated workflow and is therefore NOT claimed as an observed outcome of this experiment (see prereg 6.E). A MEASUREMENT_INVALID is declared if python/git tooling needed for those commands is unavailable.
Counter honesty: model_calls and model_tokens are asserted 0; no counter events are injected; only the kernel's own TrajectoryCounters surface (if used) is read.
Freeze artifacts are sha256-verified before the confirmatory measurement; any drift makes the interpretation-binding clause fail (MIXED), not silently pass.

Known threats: (1) the inferred support grammar could be broader than the generator's true support class - mitigated by declaring only same-grammar unseen positives and digit-count near-miss negatives; (2) localhost socket availability in the runner - declared a prerequisite, and an unstartable server invalidates the run rather than being scored as a negative; (3) the parameter slot name is derived structurally (doc/record) and is asserted by behavior (accept/reject), not by a hardcoded slot string.
decision_rule: Frozen rule (all clauses evaluated mechanically; see prereg.md section 6 for formulas and expected values). DR-1 treatment_identity (HARD): after landing, sha256(src/spider/kernel.py) == 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72 AND git hash-object == b15ed8487e2d1326df4ca64fb4c7b6e5a0ebf796 AND != 46929b3a951df48d7f9d1fd850871073c0d91c1868aa117e13d389fe274e8d61. DR-2 positive_roundtrip (HARD): for BOTH families, an unseen in-support identifier resolves EXECUTABLE with non-null bound_action targeting that identifier, real HTTP executes, and verify() returns True; M-PC-ROUNDTRIP-EXECUTABLE-COUNT == 2 and M-PC-ROUNDTRIP-VERIFY-COUNT == 2. DR-3 causal_ablation: B-LITERAL-ABLATION yields EXPLORE with bound_action=null for both families; M-ABLATION-LITERAL-EXECUTABLE-COUNT == 0. DR-4 known_negative_refusal (HARD): all three categories (out-of-support identifier, missing required parameter, wrong intent) are refused with bound_action=null, non-empty reason and the typed reason predicate; M-KN-REFUSAL-RATE == 1.0 and M-KN-REASON-CORRECT-COUNT == 3 out of M-KN-TOTAL == 3. DR-5 null_control: N-EMPTY-REGISTRY yields UNKNOWN with bound_action=null; M-NULL-EMPTY-EXECUTABLE-COUNT == 0. DR-6 boundary_sensitivity: PC-SUPPORT-BOUNDARY accepts both unseen in-support identifiers and refuses both near-miss out-of-support identifiers; M-BOUNDARY-ACCEPT-COUNT == 2 and M-BOUNDARY-REFUSE-COUNT == 2. DR-7 shipped_path_import: the certificate was produced by importing spider.kernel from src/ (resolved module path recorded); spider.kernel exposes distill_parameterized, resolve, verify; no vendored copy was used. DR-8 promotion_landability: the experiment delta contains only paths under {src, tests}; the landing is confined to src/spider/kernel.py (carrier bytes) plus the new tests/test_product_param_promotion.py; AND python -m compileall -q src scripts exits 0 AND python scripts/validate_repo.py exits 0 AND PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v exits 0 including the 3 pre-existing tests/test_kernel.py tests. DR-9 freeze_integrity_and_accounting: every freeze_artifact sha256 is unchanged from freeze.json.artifact_hashes AND M-MODEL-CALLS == 0 AND M-MODEL-TOKENS == 0 AND M-ABSTENTION-HTTP-REQUESTS == 0. OVERALL: SUPPORTS iff DR-1..DR-9 all PASS; FALSIFIES iff DR-1, DR-2 or DR-4 fails; MIXED iff DR-1/DR-2/DR-4 pass but any of DR-3, DR-5, DR-6, DR-7, DR-8, DR-9 fails; MEASUREMENT_INVALID iff a declared prerequisite is missing (carrier file absent or hash mismatch; landed module cannot be imported; localhost server cannot bind; required python/git tooling unavailable) - a missing prerequisite is never scored as a scientific negative.
product_consequence_positive: B1 is closed at source: the shipped src/spider/kernel.py (pinned at sha256 718efa6a... / git blob b15ed848...) exposes a parameterized mechanism that an inherited procedure visibly instantiates, executes and re-verifies on unseen in-support identifiers, with a companion known-negative refusal certificate and a binary causal ablation against the literal 0.5 path. The landing delta is authored on the Product branch within the allowed roots and passes the exact promotion-workflow validation, so the DIRECTOR can set promote_to_product=true and the sanctioned product-promote.yml can apply it to main without a manual copy. This satisfies readiness condition (1) and satisfies blocker B1's exit criteria (distill_parameterized -> resolve -> execute -> verify/UNKNOWN inside src/spider/, one known positive and one known negative, pinned shipped version), unblocking the dependent B2 task-bank and B3 capability work and the deferred four-arm C-LLM-INHERIT benchmark. It is a shipment/prerequisite result, NOT an economics or generalization result; C-PARAM-INHERIT remains EXPERIMENTAL until the deferred benchmark supplies its 'learn on A, succeed on unseen B against strong baselines' gate.
product_consequence_negative: B1 remains open and src/spider remains on the literal-only kernel at base_sha. No kernel change is proposed for promotion. The report must state the exact failing clause: if DR-1/DR-2/DR-4 fail, the carrier is not landable as-is and the gap is bounded to the landing/inducement/support-guard (not to parameterized inheritance generally, which parent EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064 established); if only DR-3/DR-5/DR-6/DR-7/DR-8/DR-9 fail, the parameterized path works but causality, boundary sensitivity, shipped-path hygiene, promotion landability or freeze integrity is unproven and must be repaired before any promotion. The smallest next action is recorded (fix packaging/import hygiene for DR-7, fix promotion-validation or test issues for DR-8, re-derive the instrument for DR-3/DR-6). No status is advanced and no promotion is authorized by a MIXED or FALSIFIES outcome.
estimated_cost: Very low. Fully local and deterministic: one 127.0.0.1 stdlib HTTP server on an ephemeral port, ~6 real HTTP POSTs (3 per family induction + 2 treatment executes), a handful of in-process resolutions, one file copy of a 19004-byte kernel plus a new test file, and three validation commands (compileall, validate_repo, unittest discover). No model calls, no external network, no browser, target wall time under a few minutes on the standard runner; single execute transaction, no sweep.
expected_information_gain: High and decisive for the program's first binding blocker. This is the first test that moves the audited parameterized carrier from an experiment-only harness copy onto the shipped import path and binds it to a binary causal ablation plus typed known-negative refusals, producing exactly the positive/negative certificates and pinned shipped version that blocker B1's exit criteria demand. A SUPPORTS outcome removes the single prerequisite that blocks readiness condition (1) and the deferred benchmark; a negative or MIXED outcome is equally informative because it bounds the residual gap to a specific clause (identity, inducement, support guard, causality, boundary, import hygiene, landability, or freeze integrity) instead of re-litigating parameterized inheritance. It also fixes the prior unreachable-branch flaw (EXP-PRODUCT-38094123727) by measuring landability via the exact promotion-workflow commands rather than claiming an out-of-process main-branch merge.

decision_rule_reachability.reason: Every DR clause has a reachable, discriminating branch on the frozen fixtures. DESIGN-time non-outcome-bearing satisfiability probes (stdlib localhost server, /tmp only, not part of the confirmatory measurement) produced: F1 induces slots {value, doc} with supports {value: ^draft\-[0-9]{1}$, doc: ^doc\-[0-9]{3}$} at confidence 0.9; unseen doc-555 -> EXECUTABLE with bound_action url .../api/docs/doc-555 and verify True; near-miss doc-55 -> EXPLORE 'out of support'; missing params -> EXPLORE 'missing required parameter'; wrong intent -> UNKNOWN 'no applicable validated mechanism'. F2 likewise (rec-999 EXECUTABLE/verify True, rec-55 refused). Literal ablation -> EXPLORE at confidence 0.5, bound_action null. Empty registry -> UNKNOWN. No arithmetic impossibility: the audited-confirmed thresholds (confidence 0.9 >= 0.8; EXECUTABLE/verify reachable) are achievable on these fixtures, and every negative path is reachable and distinguishable from the positive. The identity clause is decidable by sha256/git hash. DR-8 is decidable by exit codes of the three frozen commands. All nine clauses can individually return PASS or fail; the SUPPORTS/FALSIFIES/MIXED/MEASUREMENT_INVALID mapping is total.

measurement_prerequisites.reason: All prerequisites exist and were verified in the frozen tree at base_sha d77b4f54: the treatment source file research/experiments/EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440/harness/audited_spider/kernel.py exists with sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72 and git blob b15ed8487e2d1326df4ca64fb4c7b6e5a0ebf796; src/spider/{models.py,registry.py} are byte-identical to the carrier's, so no hidden dependency blocks the landing; src/spider/__init__.py already exports the names the certificate imports; Python 3.12 stdlib provides http.server/urllib/unittest; the repo's existing tests/test_kernel.py passes against the carrier (3/3 OK, verified in a temp package with PYTHONPATH). The only needed tooling is python and git, both standard on the runner. Missing prerequisites (carrier absent/hash mismatch, import failure, server bind failure, absent tooling) are mapped to MEASUREMENT_INVALID, not to a negative result.

baseline_identifiability.reason: The comparator is identified by code identity, not by narrative: the treatment is the landed kernel file whose sha256 must equal the carrier 718efa6a.../blob b15ed848..., while B-LITERAL-ABLATION is the same file's literal distill() path at confidence 0.5 in a fresh registry; B-PRE-LANDING-KERNEL is pinned by sha256 46929b3a.../blob cfec9866... and is used only for the before/after identity clause. All arms run on the same substrate, same fixed base_url, same intent/context/params, and the same min_confidence=0.8, so the only difference between the treatment and ablation arms is the presence/absence of parameterized induction and support guards. The design deliberately does NOT identify a baseline by trusting a favourable correctness rate under a weak comparator: the ablation is a binary code-path difference on identical inputs, which is identifiable without any ceiling/degeneracy assumption.

control_sensitivity.reason: Each control has a demonstrated contrasting state on the frozen fixtures. The literal ablation sits at the hard confidence gate (0.5 < 0.8) and returns EXPLORE with bound_action null, while the parameterized treatment returns EXECUTABLE (confidence 0.9): a one-line code-path change flips the outcome, so the control is sensitive. The empty-registry null returns UNKNOWN and cannot execute. The boundary control is two-sided: unseen doc-555/rec-999 are accepted while digit-count near-misses doc-55/rec-55 are refused with 'outside inferred support', so a trivially permissive or trivially restrictive support grammar both fail. The three known negatives span three distinct mechanisms (support guard, missing-parameter guard, intent matching) with three distinct typed reasons, so a single broken guard surfaces as a wrong reason or an EXECUTABLE. DESIGN probes confirmed all contrasting outcomes are reachable. If a control were insensitive (e.g. ablation also EXPLORABLE due to a shared bug), DR-3 would fail and the outcome would be MIXED, not a false SUPPORTS.

treatment_liveness.reason: The treatment is live and causally attributable before freeze: (a) lineage - the carrier was demonstrated live by EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064 (distill_parameterized -> resolve -> execute/verify on a real credential-free substrate) and the parent EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440 confirmed the live parameterized path in-harness while failing on a different certificate; (b) direct DESIGN-time satisfiability probes on the exact frozen fixtures produced EXECUTABLE + real HTTP execute + verify True for both families with confidence 0.9, and the exact negative/boundary/ablation/empty-registry branches; (c) the landed object is byte-identical to the audited carrier (sha256 718efa6a...), so liveness cannot be lost by the landing itself; (d) the only new code is a hermetic test that imports the shipped module via PYTHONPATH=src, which was already verified to import and pass the existing suite. This satisfies the mandate's pre-freeze executable-mechanism requirement without running the excluded four-arm benchmark.

freeze_artifacts_bound.reason: All mutable local interpretation dependencies are enumerated in freeze_artifacts and exist as repo files that the freezer will hash into freeze.json.artifact_hashes: the treatment-source oracle (carrier kernel.py), the three landed kernel dependencies that must remain unchanged through the landing (models.py, registry.py, __init__.py), and the existing regression suite (tests/test_kernel.py) whose weakening would let DR-8 pass illegitimately. The treatment target src/spider/kernel.py is intentionally NOT frozen because EXECUTE must modify it; instead its post-landing identity is pinned by the HARD DR-1 hash clause, and every other mutable dependency is frozen. Nothing outside these files can change the interpretation of the measurements.
